sam_ops_nimblepay: Hey team — since 09:02 UTC our dedicated cluster for nimblepay-prod has been returning a lot of 429s and spikes in latency. Our SLO for tokens/sec is being breached (we're seeing sustained token/sec above our committed TPS). Can you confirm if burst credits were exhausted?

alex_support: Sorry you're hitting this, Sam. Can you paste one of the error responses and the request pattern? Is this a sudden traffic spike or a change in client behavior?

sam_ops_nimblepay: Sudden spike — an A/B test sent more simultaneous batch requests. Sample response headers below (sanitized):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
content-type: application/json
x-rw-burst-credits: 0
x-rw-admission-status: rejected
x-rw-admission-reason: insufficient_headroom
x-request-id: rq_01Fxxx
```

sam_ops_nimblepay: Also seeing ~600–900ms tail latencies on 200s before the 429s. We expected burst credits to cover the test.

maria_csm: I can see the consumption curve on your Dedicated dashboard — burst credits were ~70% used by 08:58 and hit 0 around 09:04. The autoscaler added capacity at 09:10 (deploy-bot infra message below). Did you expect autoscale to trigger earlier?

ben_oncall: Tagging infra — admission_control rejecting because headroom window was too small to accept the inflight batch. Jia, can you check if we hit the per-replica token/sec limiter?

jia_infra: Confirmed. Replica-level limiter (token/sec) rate was 5k per replica; with concurrency from the A/B test we were oversubscribed. Two key things happened: 1) burst_credit balance reached zero so we fell back to strict admission control, 2) autoscale policy has a cooldown of 5m and min_replicas was set to 2, so scale-up didn't happen fast enough for that shock.

jia_infra: Quick repro we ran against the cluster (sanitized):
```
# simple repro: concurrent clients emulating NimblePay A/B
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"token-heavy prompt"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done
wait
```

alex_support: From the customer's point of view: they expected burst credits to smooth this. We should explain admission control behavior and offer mitigations.

maria_csm: Sam — immediate mitigations: 1) throttle the test client to ~70% of your committed TPS while we investigate; 2) enable request-level backoff/retry with jitter; 3) we can temporarily increase your min_replicas or bump headroom if you want us to on your Dedicated plan (short-lived). Which would you prefer?

sam_ops_nimblepay: We'd like the temporary bump to min_replicas while we re-run the test later today. Also want recommendation on headroom settings and how many burst credits we should keep for rolling tests.

jia_infra: Proposal: set min_replicas=4 for 1 hour, and set headroom_tokens equivalent to 1.5x expected peak per-second token demand for 2 minutes. That prevents immediate admission rejections during shock. We'll also advise increasing burst_credit_topup threshold for small controlled tests.

ben_oncall: Added runbook steps in thread for triage and PS. Key diagnostic queries we used (Prometheus/Grafana):
```
# tokens/sec per_replica
sum(rate(tokens_generated[1m])) by (replica)
# burst credit balance per_customer
max(burst_credit_balance{customer_id="nimblepay-prod"})
# admission rejects
sum(rate(admission_rejects_total[1m])) by (reason)
```

alex_support: Also noticed these response headers we returned to callers when admission kicks in — include them in your client logs to help triage: x-rw-burst-credits, x-rw-admission-status, x-rw-admission-reason, x-rw-replica-id.

sam_ops_nimblepay: OK will add header logging. Can you do the temporary min_replicas bump now?

jia_infra: On it. I'll open a change, apply min_replicas=4 for nimblepay-prod, and monitor. ETA ~4m.

deploy-bot: autoscaler-trigger: scale up requested for cluster nimblepay-prod, target_replicas=4, reason="manual-headroom-bump", requested_by=jia_infra at 1752106900

jia_infra: Change applied. We're monitoring CPU/GPU utilization and token/sec. So far admission rejects dropped to zero and x-rw-burst-credits stayed at 0 (no immediate top-up) but traffic is now accepted because headroom is available.

maria_csm: Follow-ups for the customer: 1) long-term: consider raising committed capacity or a standing headroom agreement for predictable test windows; 2) schedule load test with Redwood SRE so we can pre-warm burst credits; 3) tighten client-side concurrency for uncontrolled A/B spikes.

sam_ops_nimblepay: Thanks — please also include a short doc on how burst credits work and the rule for autoscale cooldowns. Our infra team will coordinate a time to run a controlled test with you.

alex_support: Will share a concise FAQ and a recommended config snippet. For reference: current autoscale cooldown=5m, per_replica_limit=5k tokens/sec, default_burst_bucket=120k tokens. We'll put tailored numbers in the doc for NimblePay.

ben_oncall: Marking this thread as escalated -> support-incident ticket created: SI-2025-339. Owner: alex_support. Next steps: follow up with a postmortem if we see repeat incidents.

sam_ops_nimblepay: Appreciate the fast help. I'll pause the A/B run for now and we can schedule the controlled run after your doc. :thumbsup:

alex_support: Thanks all — logging notes to ticket and will attach graphs + the repro curl snippets. If anything degrades ping @ben_oncall.
